description: Write and maintain a project's Architecture Decision Record log — the files, not just the prose. Every change to the log carries invariants a hand edit breaks silently: the next number must be monotonic, the filename must be NNNN-slug.md derived from the title, a supersede touches two files and rewrites the old one's Status section only (never its body), and adr-tools plus Structurizr's !adrs importer parse the exact English literals (Date:, ## Status / ## Context / ## Decision / ## Consequences, the status words) even when the prose is in another language. Michael Nygard format, file-compatible with Nat Pryce's adr-tools, .adr-dir discovery. Use this skill for any work on a decision log — including the operations that look like a one-line edit: "write an ADR", "document this decision", "we decided to use X over Y", "ADR 7 is out of date, mark it superseded and write the replacement", "amend the existing record", "we changed our minds about Z", "start a decision log" — even if the user never says "ADR".

results.query: we finally settled the debate — we're going with Postgres instead of DynamoDB for the orders service because of the relational reporting needs. can you capture this so the team has a record of why?
write a full design doc for the new notification service — problem statement, the approaches we considered, trade-offs, rollout plan
draw a sequence diagram of how the auth handshake works between the SPA, the BFF and Keycloak
create the C4 container diagram for our payments platform in a workspace.dsl
link all our existing ADRs from doc/adr into the Structurizr architecture docs so they show up in the decision log view
write up the postmortem for yesterday's outage, including timeline and action items
document our REST API endpoints so the frontend team knows the request/response shapes
we need a PRD for the new self-serve onboarding flow — goals, user stories, success metrics
what's the difference between an ADR and an RFC? when should i use each?
summarize the key decisions we made in last week's architecture review meeting into meeting notes
help me decide whether to use Kafka or RabbitMQ for our event bus — walk me through the trade-offs
